articles.title: Some of Mexico's beach towns are losing tourists. Experts suggest heading inland.
articles.summary: Fewer travelers are taking vacations to Mexico's beach towns, due in part to increased seaweed and higher flight prices.
articles.body:
Some of Mexico's most famous beach destinations are seeing fewer international flights — and visitors.

United Airlines made headlines last month when it announced it would stop serving Tulum International Airport in the Riviera Maya region along the Caribbean Sea. The flights are scheduled to end in January 2027.

But it's not the only airline slashing service to Tulum. Aeroméxico, American Airlines, Delta, JetBlue, WestJet and Volaris are all canceling or reducing flight frequency here.

The news comes shortly after the Financial Times reported that international traffic at the nearby Cancún International Airport was down by almost 12% year-over-year in September, while international arrivals in Puerto Vallarta, a beach town in western Mexico, declined by 19%.

Jessica Upton, founder and luxury travel adviser at J. Upton Travel, a Virtuoso Agency, tells Yahoo Travel she's seen a "significant decline" in inquiries into Mexico's typically popular beach towns this year. While she still has clients traveling to the Riviera Maya and Cabo later in 2026, she says those trips were primarily planned in 2025. "We haven't received nearly as many new inquiries for [Mexican beach trips] in 2026 compared to what we've seen in the past," she explains.

So, why are fewer people visiting the area?

Upton says one reason could be the uptick in flight prices to Mexico, noting that "the cost of airfare to some of these destinations has increased to the point that flights can be comparable to, or sometimes even more expensive than flying to certain Caribbean destinations."

"When travelers are looking at the overall cost of a vacation, that aspect can make other destinations more appealing," she says.

While the higher price of jet fuel means airlines are passing those costs on to their customers, fewer flights into Mexico could also lead to higher prices overall for the routes that do serve the area.

And while hotel prices have "leveled out," Upton hasn't seen a dramatic decline in accommodation rates in the area, which could have offset the higher airfare.

Plus, thanks to the stronger peso , Americans now have weaker buying power in Mexico than in previous years, meaning people may think twice about visiting an area once known for more budget-friendly beach vacations.

The Caribbean coast of Mexico has also seen one of its worst seasons for sargassum , a seaweed that is both smelly and unsightly along the shoreline. And Puerto Vallarta suffered reputationally as a tourist destination after February 2026 cartel violence led to a shelter-in-place order for the area. Most recently, Mexico introduced a new amendment mandating that tourism providers obtain documentation verifying that travelers have parental or legal authority over minors they're traveling with. Though not inherently a deterrent, it could be a hardship for travelers with imminent plans to visit Mexico who don't have the necessary documents in order.

It's important to note that not all of Mexico (including other beach areas) is seeing a decline.

Stephen McGillivray, chief partner marketing officer for Internova Travel Group, tells Yahoo Travel that there are still certain things enticing visitors to the area. "While demand varies by destination, we're seeing strong interest in emerging resort areas such as Playa Mujeres, north of Cancún, and continued growth in Cabo," he says. "New luxury resort development is also driving interest, particularly among travelers seeking elevated all-inclusive experiences."

But if you want to go beyond the typical destinations in Mexico, there are many great options.

Ben Gritzewsky, a travel adviser and Mexico specialist at VEN, a member of Frosch by Chase Travel, tells Yahoo Travel that he recommends Mérida, the capital and largest city of the Yucatán state in southeastern Mexico. While you can visit the Gulf side beaches, you can also visit the mangrove forests.

"The whole peninsula is covered with fascinating attractions and sights, and a lot of natural wonders," he says. "Very close to Mérida is one of the most important flamingo sanctuaries in the world. In season, you can go on a boat ride and see thousands of flamingos. "

Good Horizon founder Meagan Drillinger, a travel adviser and Mexico specialist, tells Yahoo Travel she also recommends Mérida to people seeking something a bit different, noting that the area has a historic city center with excellent food and a ring of restored haciendas just outside town.

"It's also a good base for the Gulf coast, which most foreign visitors skip," she says. "Progreso is about 30 minutes away, and the quieter fishing towns of Sisal and Celestun are a little further."

Another place both Gritzewsky and Drillinger recommend is Oaxaca City, which is "a foodie capital of Mexico, known for its moles, markets and mezcal," Drillinger says.

"The historic center is walkable, with stunning, brightly colored buildings, and mountains are never out of view," she adds. She also recommends a visit to the Templo de Santo Domingo de Guzmán, a 16th-century Roman Catholic church and former monastery with a gilded interior. You can also drive out of the city to visit the Zapotec ruins at Monte Albán.

Gritzewsky says this area is also less expensive than Cancún, which can make it more appealing to visitors. Plus, "there are coffee plantations and outdoor activities of all kinds, and several resort areas along the Pacific coast of Oaxaca."

articles.title: 'May have sent 1,500 in India': US techie held in Tamil Nadu likely behind dozens of Mumbai bomb threats, say cops
articles.summary: US-based techie Sharath Shankar detained in Tamil Nadu for allegedly sending 1,500 hoax bomb threat emails targeting Mumbai sites; police probe motive and links.
articles.body: MUMBAI: City police believe that a 28-year-old techie who was working in the US is behind dozens of recent emails warning of attacks at the BMC office, Metro stations, Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), various courts, schools, film star Amitabh Bachchan’s bungalow and vital installations.The man, Sharath Subramanian Shankar, who hails from Tamil Nadu’s Tirunelveli district, was detained at the Chennai airport by the state’s anti-terrorism squad (ATS) in July on his arrival, based on intelligence provided by Mumbai police.He is currently in Tamil Nadu police’s custody. He is suspected to have sent 1,500 hoax emails to various agencies in the country in the last two years.“Once we obtain his custody, we will thoroughly interrogate him to determine the reason for sending the threats,” said a senior Mumbai police officer.A Mumbai police officer, who was part of the threats probe, had trapped Shankar while communicating with him following a lead from one of his emails.To one of his leading questions, Shankar, who didn’t know that he was communicating with a policeman, replied from his personal email ID. It was sufficient for Mumbai police to collect information about him. That was shared with Tamil Nadu police, and Shankar was arrested on his return from the US.Every threat mail in Mumbai triggered a set protocol of evacuation of the premises and tightening of security, including deployment of bomb detection and disposal squads, sniffer dog squads, and local and crime branch police personnel.In some cases, public services were disrupted. All of the threats turned out to be hoaxes.Before Shankar’s arrest, a set of threat emails was sent to BSE on June 10, claiming that RDX had been planted inside the building. The mails came from different accounts using various VPNs and other anonymising technologies to conceal the sender’s identity and to make digital tracing extremely difficult. Sources said the probe was delayed because of this.The role of another suspect, Ankit Shankhwar (24), who was arrested by the Uttar Pradesh ATS, is also under investigation. He was nabbed for running a network involved in creating and supplying fake email accounts.An initial probe by the UP ATS found that email IDs created by him were used to send hoax bomb threats to several prominent establishments in Mumbai on Nov 12, the agency has claimed.The UP ATS said the accused sold the email IDs to a Bangladesh national, and these accounts were later used to send threat emails to several locations in Mumbai.The ATS has claimed that Shankhwar received $50,000 (around Rs 47 lakh) from sources in countries such as Turkiye and Egypt in connection with the supply of these email accounts. Mumbai police are yet to ascertain his role.The criminal intelligence unit of Mumbai crime branch and local police stations are also conducting separate investigations. articles.title: Jensen Huang: How the Nvidia scandal exposed the risks of Asia's big AI bet
articles.summary: Asian stocks have been on a rollercoaster ride after Jensen Huang's shock return as Nvidia CEO.
articles.body:
Jensen Huang's extraordinary return as Nvidia's boss rocked not only its shares in New York but also sent shockwaves through the artificial intelligence (AI) industry around the world.

Those jolts were felt particularly in Asia as the saga highlighted the region's huge exposure to the technology.

Tech-heavy stock indexes in Japan, South Korea and Taiwan went on a rollercoaster ride this week. Markets soared after a near-trillion dollar surge in Nvidia's share price but then slumped as concerns about political and regulatory scrutiny hit investor confidence.

The chipmaker is a "symbolic bellwether" of the AI trade that is fast becoming key to places like South Korea, Taiwan, Singapore and Malaysia," says Dylan Loh, an international studies lecturer at Nanyang Technological University.

From chip manufacturing to data centres to foreign investments, AI has become a strategic priority for these economies - and they are now increasingly dependent on Nvidia's fortunes.

In Nvidia, the AI industry has the unrivalled power of cutting-edge chips and the financial clout that turned it into "the bank of AI". And in Huang, it has a high-profile evangelist.

That combination has put it at the heart of the AI ecosystem in more ways than one.

For one, Nvidia was able to grow rapidly by outsourcing chip production instead of having to spend heavily to build its own manufacturing plants.

It contracts out most of its production to Taiwanese chipmaking giant TSMC.

That means Taiwan is vulnerable to changes in AI tech demand, says Paul Cavey, founder of Taipei-based research firm East Asia Econ.

"The surge in [Taiwan's] real economic growth since 2024 has been because of the big increase in AI related exports".

Huang said earlier this year that Nvidia plans to invest around $150bn (£114.4bn) a year in Taiwan at a launch to celebrate the firm's planned headquarters on the island.

To a lesser extent, South Korea and Japan are also exposed to the industry, Cavey adds. They are among its suppliers of key components such as memory chips and testing equipment, with firms like Samsung and SK Hynix making the firm's processors.

On top of that, Nvidia is a financial backstop and major lender to companies in the AI supply chain.

It is difficult to overstate the role Nvidia, with Huang at its helm, has played in the region's AI industry. Nvidia's chips fill its data centres, power its AI models and feed the companies making cars and electronics.

"Asia isn't just a customer base for Nvidia. It is an indispensable engine of the company's AI dominance because of East Asia's semiconductor manufacturing and memory ecosystems," Loh says.

In the Asia-Pacific region, the data centre market, which is largely powered by Nvidia chips, is in the midst of an "unprecedented boom", according to property services firm CBRE . The volume of investment has been rising steadily in recent years to reach a record of $11.6bn (£8.85bn) in 2025.

In South East Asia, Singapore-based AI company Megaspeed had become the region's biggest buyer of Nvidia chips before it was accused of smuggling them to China. Megaspeed has said it "conducts legitimate and lawful business" and has "retained external legal counsel to conduct a thorough internal investigation".

The US has said it intends to ban Megaspeed Ltd from doing business in the United States.

But in a timely example of the importance of AI to this region, Singapore this week further raised its growth forecast for this year as the technology boosts its economy.

The world's biggest tech firms - Google, Microsoft, Oracle - also plan to boost their spending on infrastructure in the region by roughly 60% this year, CBRE added.

The demand for neoclouds, which are specialised data centres which power AI, has also risen rapidly, it said.

For economies betting heavily on AI, Nvidia has become "hugely important", with vast sums being spent on its chips and factory activity increasingly dependent on its technology, Loh told the BBC.

In many economies, news of Huang's return to Nvidia was met with jubilation.

In Taiwan, where he was born and the home of "Jensanity", investors jokingly described his return as a "one man saves the village" story.

Social media and groups on messaging platform Line saw posts like "Old Huang is back," while some investors said "Daddy is back to save my life" and "the humanitarian corridor is open."

However, some said the episode should also prompt a closer look at how effective Taiwan has been in building a "non-China" semiconductor supply chain, and how risks from the industry's heavy reliance on Nvidia should be managed better.

Asia's technology industry has been under increasing pressure from the US in recent years. The administrations of both Joe Biden and Donald Trump have tightened rules on the export of Nvidia's most advanced chips to China.

Those efforts seem to have been renewed. Just last week, Washington announced new rules that will increase scrutiny of data centre operators in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil.

The latest move not only restricts the export of high-end chips to China, but also access to their computing power, which Chinese firms currently rent abroad to train AI models.

This will hit South East Asian countries, which have invested billions in data centre infrastructure to cater to Chinese firms. Nvidia has already paused shipments to the region, according to the Financial Times, although it is unclear if this is only a temporary move while it figures out how to comply with the new export rules.

Nvidia did not immediately respond to a BBC request for comment.

Then there is the growing bipartisan backlash against President Trump and Nvidia after he said he "made the deal" to "convince" the company‘s board to reinstate Huang.

Huang is also due to testify before Congress next week. And as Democrats prepare to take control of the US House and Senate in the New Year, Huang is likely to face further risks.

"Jensen's return may resolve the immediate leadership crisis, but it does not resolve the legal and political overhangs," said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist from Saxo Bank.

Investor concerns about the trillions of dollars being poured into AI and the pivotal role Nvidia plays in the industry were already sending tremors through global stock markets.

Some fear that while the company and its charismatic leader have been crucial in driving AI's growth that concentration of influence also poses a threat.

Especially now when it appears that Huang's future - which is still uncertain - could impact economies that are heavily exposed to the AI industry.

"I would say the President and White House would love to brush this over and say its fine but I believe Democrats in Congress will definitely be probing", Ray Wang, founder of San Francisco-based Constellation Research said.

"The story is not over yet... Jensen coming back is probably the biggest, baddest return ever. The question is what will happen next?"

Additional reporting by Benny Lu, BBC Chinese

articles.title: Trademark Dan Campbell fourth-down gamble backfires, opening door to stunning Bears comeback victory
articles.summary: Caleb Williams hit Rome Odunze for a six-yard touchdown with three seconds left as the Chicago Bears stole first place in the NFC North from Detroit.
articles.body: The legend of Dan Campbell took a hit this Thanksgiving Day. A new legend might be growing around Chicago Bears coach Ben Johnson. When Chicago Bears coaches and players met on Thanksgiving eve to discuss Thursday's game against the Detroit Lions, Johnson drove the conversation toward taking stuff from the Lions. The Lions were the division leaders. They've been the NFC North's most consistently successful team for years. CALEB WILLIAMS, WHO ONCE SEEMED TO DISRESPECT NATIONAL ANTHEM, SHOWED PATRIOTISM ON THANKSGIVING "They were at the top of the division," Johnson said. "They had what we wanted." And the Bears went and got it. Now they are the NFC North's leaders and de facto best team in one of the league's best divisions. But not before it was all delivered in electric fashion. Caleb Williams connected with wide receiver Rome Odunze, who was not the primary receiver on the play, in the back corner of the end zone for a six-yard touchdown with three seconds to play to give the Bears the winning score. "Absolutely incredible," CBS play-by-play voice Jim Nantz said, describing the moment. And it was that because the TD gave the Bears their first lead of the game after the Lions led for 59:57. It gave Williams – who had a viral moment during the national anthem – his first career victory over the Bears. The Lions swept the Bears the first two years the third-year Chicago quarterback has been in the league. "This shows how far we've come in the last year-and-a-half," Johnson said. "Proud of the offense the way they handled that last drive." NICK FOLES BELIEVES BEARS ARE TEAM TO BEAT IN LOADED NFC NORTH: 'SOMETHING'S BREWING IN CHICAGO' This result meant the Lions wasted a Herculean performance by Jahmyr Gibbs. He rushed for 205 yards. He averaged 9.8 yards per carry. He scored three touchdowns. And it wasn't enough. "They did what they had to do to win that game," Campbell said. Stunning stuff. As the Bears walked off the field to a Turducken celebration in honor of John Madden – a tribute the NFL set for all three Thursday games – Campbell had to be beating himself up. Chicago's game winning score, you see, came after the Lions' coach passed on a 51-yard field goal attempt by his long-range kicker Jake Bates. With 2:22 to play, Campbell gambled on closing out the game by going for it on fourth-and-4 from the Bears' 33 yard line. Quarterback Jared Goff completed his attempt to Gibbs but the running back was stopped after only a one-yard gain. This was a deeply controversial decision, although not to Campbell. "I thought we'd get it, I mean, first of all," Campbell said. "I really believed we were going to get that." Bates has been something a long-range assassin for the Lions in his time as their kicker. He has connected on 12 of 20 field goals of 50 yards or more. He has converted seven field goals of 56 yards or more. He has four career field goals of 58 yards. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! Letting him try that long field goal was not easy to dismiss. "I don't regret that," Campbell said. "I wish we'd have made that but sometimes that happens, you know?" Yes, we know. We saw. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: Iran accuses Zelenskyy of 'false flag' Kuwait drone strike op to get Trump's attention
articles.summary: A former Iran nuclear adviser claimed Thursday the Kuwait drone attack was a Ukrainian "false flag" staged to get President Donald Trump's attention.
articles.body: A former adviser to Iran's nuclear negotiating team accused Ukraine on Thursday of orchestrating a deadly drone attack in Kuwait to prove its worth to President Donald Trump, as Tehran continued to deny responsibility. And while Kuwaiti and Italian officials blamed Iran for the strike, which killed two Italian defense technicians and wounded two others, Iran’s embassy in Rome warned against "false flag" operations it said were aimed at widening the Persian Gulf conflict and now drawing Europe into the crisis. Mohammad Marandi, who served as an adviser during talks with the U.S. in Pakistan and has been dubbed Iran's "English-language mouthpiece," claimed Ukrainian forces were operating across the Middle East, including in northern Iraq and Syria, also in remarks reported by the Fars News Agency, which is affiliated with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). IRAN TARGETS US AIR BASE IN KUWAIT AFTER US DEFENSIVE STRIKES AMID CRITICISM FROM GULF STATES "It is widely believed in Iran that the attack on Kuwait was a false flag operation, likely carried out by the Ukrainian regime, because its operatives are now present across the region, including in northern Iraq and Syria. Ukraine aims to demonstrate its potential to Trump," Marandi said on X. Fars also cited a security source who claimed Ukrainian operatives had deployed thousands of drones and other unmanned aircraft in several Middle Eastern countries, including Iraq's Kurdistan region, according to Iran International. Kuwait's Defense Ministry said falling debris from the interception of Iranian drones struck a military facility Thursday, initially wounding four people. Two Italian nationals later died of their injuries. A Kuwaiti national and a Pakistani national were also wounded and taken to a hospital for treatment. The ministry did not disclose the facility's precise location. Italy's Foreign Ministry confirmed that the two Italian nationals were employees of Rheinmetall Italia, the Italian subsidiary of German defense manufacturer Rheinmetall. "An explosion caused by a drone attack ... occurred at a site where two Italian technicians from the company Rheinmetall Italia were working," the ministry said in a statement. The victims were identified as Antonio Saccoccio, 65, of Formia, Italy, and Emanuele Lo Russo, 36, of Rome, Italian news agency ANSA reported. EUROPE ASSASSINATION SCHEME EMERGES AS IRAN DENIES DC 'DIRTY BOMB' PLOT AMID TRUMP WARNING The men had been performing maintenance on detection antennas for the Skyguard air defense system. Iran's embassy in Rome rejected allegations that Tehran was responsible for the attack, warning of alleged efforts to draw European countries into the Middle East conflict. "The Embassy of the Islamic Republic of Iran also draws the international community's attention to 'false flag' activities and operations aimed at expanding the scope of the conflict, linking disputes in other regions to the Persian Gulf crisis, drawing Europe into the crisis, and exacerbating the current critical situation, and calls on everyone to remain vigilant in this regard." Meanwhile, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said he had spoken with his Italian and Kuwaiti counterparts and offered to cooperate in an investigation into the deadly incident. "In calls with my Italian and Kuwaiti counterparts, expressed condolences over deaths of Italian citizens in Kuwait," Araghchi wrote. "The incident is suspicious and looks like a precooked recipe for war. "We stand ready to cooperate with Kuwait and Italy to determine the cause of the incident," he added. TOP GULF OFFICIAL OFFERS GLIMMER OF HOPE ON TRUMP-IRAN NUCLEAR TALKS AS THREAT OF WAR HANGS OVER REGION Kuwait, a key U.S. ally in the Persian Gulf, has repeatedly come under Iranian attack since the U.S. and Israel launched military operations against Iran on Feb. 28. Ukraine has deployed drone specialists and interceptor drones to the Middle East to help defend against Iranian attacks, expanding its regional defense cooperation by sharing technology and military expertise developed during its war with Russia. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in March that Kyiv had sent interceptor drones and specialists to help protect U.S. military installations in Jordan at Washington's request. Ukraine also announced that teams of military specialists had been deployed to Kuwait, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia to help defend against Iranian drone attacks. articles.title: Hostel reúne arte, turismo e vista privilegiada no Rio de Janeiro | G1
articles.standfirst: Espaço na comunidade Tavares Bastos reúne hospedagem, museu, mirante e mosaicos feitos por visitantes de dezenas de países; negócio também ajuda a movimentar a economia local.
articles.summary: Com mosaicos produzidos por visitantes de dezenas de países, espaço na Tavares Bastos movimenta o turismo e os negócios da comunidade.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

O que começou como a casa de um inglês apaixonado pelo Rio de Janeiro se transformou em um dos pontos turísticos mais singulares da capital fluminense.

Localizado na comunidade Tavares Bastos, na Zona Sul da cidade, o espaço criado por Bob Nadkarni reúne hostel, galeria de arte, museu e mirante, atraindo visitantes brasileiros e estrangeiros em busca de uma experiência que mistura cultura, história e convivência.

Escultor, cineasta e jornalista, Nadkarni chegou ao Rio no início da década de 1980 e se encantou com a vista privilegiada da Baía de Guanabara.

A paixão pela cidade o levou a se estabelecer no alto do morro, onde começou a transformar a própria residência em um espaço de encontro para viajantes . Com o passar dos anos, o local ganhou fama e se tornou referência para quem busca um turismo mais autêntico e próximo da vida carioca.

A principal marca do empreendimento nasceu de uma ideia simples. Após a sugestão de um hóspede, paredes, escadarias e corredores começaram a ser revestidos por mosaicos produzidos pelos próprios visitantes.

O projeto cresceu e, atualmente, reúne obras criadas por artistas, turistas e voluntários de dezenas de países , transformando o hostel em uma galeria de arte coletiva e em constante transformação.

Hostel criado por inglês vira atração turística e galeria de arte no Rio de Janeiro — Foto: Reprodução/PEGN

Hoje, o negócio é administrado por Marluce Feitosa, conhecida como Malu, que assumiu a missão de preservar o legado deixado pelo fundador.

Além da hospedagem, o espaço oferece visitas guiadas e café da manhã aberto ao público , atividades que ajudam a sustentar a operação e ampliar a experiência dos visitantes.

"Eu sou a Malu. E o meu negócio é mostrar o mundo através da arte", resume a empreendedora.

Segundo ela, o impacto da iniciativa vai muito além do próprio hostel. O aumento do fluxo de turistas ajuda a movimentar a economia da comunidade, beneficiando serviços como mototáxis, kombis, bares, padarias e pequenos comércios locais.

O espaço também já serviu de cenário para produções audiovisuais e recebeu visitantes de diversos países, contribuindo para consolidar a Tavares Bastos como um destino turístico no Rio de Janeiro.

Mesmo após a morte de Bob Nadkarni, em 2023, o projeto continua crescendo . Novos mosaicos seguem sendo instalados e o espaço permanece aberto à participação de artistas e visitantes.

"Enquanto tiver parede livre, a gente vai dar continuidade", afirma Malu. "A arte nunca termina por aqui."

articles.title: Luara Fonseca relata erro em diagnóstico de bipolaridade | G1
articles.standfirst: Influenciadora de 21 anos contou que a vida "mudou radicalmente" desde que foi diagnosticada com Transtorno de Personalidade Obsessivo-Compulsiva (TPOC) e começou o tratamento correto.
articles.summary: Influenciadora de 21 anos contou que a vida "mudou radicalmente" desde que foi diagnosticada com Transtorno de Personalidade Obsessivo-Compulsiva (TPOC).
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

A influenciadora Luara Fonseca, de 21 anos, revelou que o diagnóstico de transtorno bipolar, divulgado nas redes sociais em maio , estava errado. Em uma nova publicação na internet, a jovem contou que sua vida "mudou radicalmente" após receber o diagnóstico de Transtorno de Personalidade Obsessivo-Compulsiva (TPOC) e iniciar o tratamento adequado com medicação.

Luara nasceu em Santos , no litoral de São Paulo, e começou a criar conteúdo na internet aos 10 anos. Atualmente, a jovem soma mais de 40 milhões de seguidores nas redes sociais.

Em maio, a influenciadora usou as redes sociais para divulgar que havia sido diagnosticada com transtorno de bipolaridade tipo 2 e pretendia usar a influência para conscientizar as pessoas sobre a condição.

Na quarta-feira (25), no entanto, Luara voltou a falar sobre saúde mental e compartilhou que não é bipolar, mas tem TPOC. Em um vídeo sobre o assunto, ela disse ter ficado "revoltada" com o erro no diagnóstico.

Luara Fonseca revelou diagnóstico de TPOC — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais

"Eu vivi experiências assustadoras e extremamente antiéticas ao longo desses 7 anos em busca do meu diagnóstico. TPOC é um transtorno altamente negligenciado, e isso me espanta. Penso que tantas pessoas estão desamparadas agora, assim como eu estava", escreveu na legenda do vídeo.

A influenciadora também afirmou que sua vida mudou para melhor após o início do tratamento correto. Ela pretende usar a visibilidade para alertar a população sobre a importância de escolher com cuidado os profissionais responsáveis pelo diagnóstico.

No vídeo, Luara explicou que a obsessão foi confundida com episódios de mania, caracterizados por humor anormalmente elevado, expansivo ou irritável, que podem ocorrer no transtorno bipolar.

Ela contou que era "extremista" e sentia cansaço excessivo, mas, quando começava uma gravação, não parava para comer ou descansar.

"Então eu começava e aí eu virava a noite. Foi por i sso que veio aí o suposto diagnóstico de bipolaridade, porque às vezes eu ficava sem dormir, mas não era mania, era obsessão . Isso não ser investigado a fundo me deixou muito revoltada, mas enfim, agora já foi", explicou.

De acordo com a influenciadora, os transtornos são bem distintos. "Realmente eu não me encaixava em nada na bipolaridade, tirando os sintomas que na verdade eram TPOC", ressaltou.

Luara Fonseca, de 21 anos, revelou ter recebido o diagnóstico de transtorno bipolar tipo 2 — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Transtorno bipolar: se destaca através das alterações do humor, entre períodos de depressão e de euforia [do grego, 'mania'] ou sentimentos mistos. As fases são bem definidas e têm duração de dias ou até meses.

TPOC: caracterizado por preocupação generalizada com organização, perfeccionismo e controle que interferem na conclusão de tarefas.

Luara disse que era uma "adulta muito disfuncional" por ser excessivamente perfeccionista. Por isso, precisava marcar apenas um compromisso por dia e, dependendo da demanda, não podia agendar nada na véspera ou no dia seguinte.

Segundo a influenciadora, o comportamento também provocava muito cansaço. Em alguns momentos, ela precisava interromper todas as atividades e ficar de cama. A jovem chegou, inclusive, a recusar alguns serviços de publicidade.

Por outro lado, quando começava uma tarefa, não conseguia parar até concluí-la. " Eu ficava tão obsessiva que eu não conseguia fazer nada. Então eu não conseguia comer, eu não conseguia tomar água . Se eu estava gravando há, sei lá, sete horas, eu tranquilamente estava sete horas sem tomar água, sete horas sem comer e sete horas sem parar e sem dormir", relembrou.

Luara também contou que era muito extremista e imaginava grandes consequências para qualquer erro. Além disso, tinha uma obsessão por simetria. "E parecia o quê? Que eu só era uma pessoa chata, uma pessoa fútil, que pensava o tempo todo na aparência, mas, na verdade, eu estava em sofrimento", afirmou.

A influenciadora disse ainda que tinha o hábito de refletir constantemente sobre diferentes assuntos. "Eu fazia reflexão sobre tudo o tempo inteiro na minha cabeça", ressaltou, explicando que questionava tudo até chegar a um estado melancólico e depressivo.

Ainda no vídeo, a jovem contou que sua vida mudou drasticamente nos últimos meses e que não se importa mais com as coisas como antes. "A única coisa que silenciou esses pensamentos foi a medicação", esclareceu.

Luara Fonseca, de 21 anos, começou na internet em 2015 — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Luara Fonseca nasceu em 2005 e começou na internet aos 10 anos, mas ganhou projeção nacional durante a pandemia de covid-19, tornando-se uma das maiores criadoras de conteúdo digital do Brasil.

Hoje, ela soma 4,16 milhões de inscritos no YouTube, 23 milhões de seguidores no TikTok, 13,1 milhões no Instagram e 1 milhão no Threads, onde compartilha conteúdos de lifestyle, humor, dança e beleza. Durante a carreira digital, Luara já lançou diversos produtos e até estrelou o filme de comédia "Partiu América".

O g1 entrou em contato com a equipe da influenciadora, mas não obteve retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

articles.title: Navio de cruzeiro 'invade' trânsito em Santos em ilusão de ótica | G1
articles.standfirst: Imagens mostram cruzeiro chegando ao Porto de Santos (SP) com efeito visual que confundiu internautas. Autor disse que 'escondeu' o mar de propósito para criar a cena.
articles.summary: Imagens mostram cruzeiro chegando ao Porto de Santos (SP) com efeito visual que confundiu internautas. Autor disse que 'escondeu' o mar de propósito para criar a cena.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Um vídeo mostra um navio de cruzeiro chegando ao Porto de Santos , no litoral de São Paulo. O ângulo em que as imagens foram gravadas dá a impressão de que a enorme embarcação 'invadiu' o trânsito da cidade (assista acima) .

O registro foi feito por Anderson Coelho, por volta das 7h40 de quinta-feira (26). Ao g1 , ele contou ter 'escondido' o mar propositalmente, criando uma ilusão de ótica para parecer que o navio MSC Musica estava andando com os carros na Avenida Rei Pelé, no bairro Ponta da Praia.

Navio de cruzeiro parece 'invadir' trânsito em Santos, SP — Foto: Imagens cedidas por @aquituvedecima

Anderson é piloto de drone e faz vídeos diários para a página "Aqui TU vê de cima". Desta vez, ele decidiu usar o próprio celular Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra e alcançou milhares de visualizações. Veja abaixo as reações dos internautas:

👤"O trânsito mais lindo do mundo 😍". 👤"Um dia passearei em um destes... 🛳😍❤️🙌". 👤"Eu estava nele ❤️😍 a melhor viagem da vidaaaaaa".

Na época, o chefe do departamento de Física Aplicada do Instituto de Física da Universidade de São Paulo (USP), Paulo Artaxo, falou sobre ilusão de ótica.

"A foto foi tirada com [uma lente] teleobjetiva que comprime o campo visual", dando assim a impressão de que o navio está entre os prédios, segundo ele. O mesmo aconteceu neste caso em que a embarcação parece estar invadindo o trânsito.

Já o especialista em Física Rodolfo Bonafim, que também tem especializações em Climatologia, Astronomia e Geologia, explicou como os recursos fotográficos alteram a percepção humana em determinadas imagens.

"Quando você usa o 'zoom' de uma lente, ou seja, quando aproxima um objeto de uma forma 'artificial', o fundo vai parecer mais próximo. Isso diminui todas as distâncias pela mesma proporção", acrescentou Rodolfo.

Segundo a empresa responsável, o MSC Musica conta com um grande teatro, além de diversos bares e lounges com apresentações de música ao vivo. Os hóspedes também podem aproveitar piscinas, hidromassagens, spa, academia, minigolfe, pista de caminhada e quadra poliesportiva.

A embarcação passou por uma série de aprimoramentos antes de chegar no Brasil para a temporada de cruzeiros 2026/2027. Entre as melhorias, estão a inclusão do MSC Yacht Club, uma área privativa de luxo, além da repaginação do spa e uma nova academia.

Na gastronomia, as novidades incluem dois restaurantes de especialidade, sendo um inspirado nas tradicionais churrascarias americanas e o outro especializado na culinária asiática.

Nesta temporada, o navio oferece mini cruzeiros de três e quatro noites, com embarques em Santos, e visitas alternadas em Búzios, Ilha Grande e Ilhabela.

Já os itinerários de sete noites sairão do Rio de Janeiro e passarão por Búzios, Ilhabela, Ilha Grande, Itajaí e Paranaguá. Também será possível embarcar nas últimas duas cidades citadas.

articles.title: Noivo desmaia duas vezes em casamento em SC e vídeo viraliza | G1
articles.standfirst: Agricultor de 36 anos disse que não estava nervoso antes de entrar na igreja. Padrinhos e mãe ajudaram a socorrê-lo em meio a cerimônia na igreja em Jaraguá do Sul.
articles.summary: Agricultor de 36 anos disse que não estava nervoso antes de entrar na igreja. Padrinhos e mãe ajudaram a socorrê-lo em meio a cerimônia na igreja em Jaraguá do Sul.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

O noivo que desmaiou duas vezes durante a própria cerimônia de casamento, em Jaraguá do Sul , no Norte de Santa Catarina , contou o que sentiu antes de passar mal e como reagiu ao descobrir que o vídeo do momento havia viralizado nas redes sociais .

Em entrevista ao g1 , Jonathan Vogel, de 36 anos, disse que não estava nervoso antes de entrar na igreja. Segundo ele, conversava normalmente com os familiares e padrinhos até o início da cerimônia, quando começou a sentir um desconforto físico.

"Uma leve dor na perna e começou um calor de baixo para cima. Até que eu senti que ia passar mal e avisei a Luana [noiva]", relatou.

O casamento com Luana de Sousa Vogel aconteceu no sábado (21), em uma igreja luterana de Jaraguá do Sul. Os dois episódios foram registrados pela equipe de filmagem contratada pelo casal.

O vídeo do noivo perdendo as forças e sendo amparado pelos padrinhos, viralizou nas redes sociais. Até esta quinta-feira (26), o registro acumulava mais de 1,3 milhão de visualizações.

Jonathan contou que percebeu que estava prestes a desmaiar, mas não se lembra de ter perdido a consciência durante o primeiro episódio.

Na segunda vez em que começou a passar mal, os sinais foram semelhantes. A solução foi continuar a cerimônia sentado.

"Começou a baixar a pressão e daí decidimos continuar sentados na cerimônia", explicou.

Casal Luana e Jonathan continuou cerimônia de casamento sentado após noivo desmaiar em Jaraguá do Sul, SC — Foto: Montagem/Arquivo pessoal/Reprodução/Daniel Filmes

Apesar de não ter se sentido nervoso antes de entrar na igreja, Jonathan acredita que a emoção do momento pode ter contribuído para os episódios. Ele afirmou que nunca havia desmaiado antes .

"Eu nunca tinha desmaiado, mas acho que pode ser que foi nervosismo mesmo", disse.

A situação chamou a atenção nas redes sociais, e o noivo afirmou que achou estranho ver o próprio casamento repercutindo tanto na internet.

"Foi meio estranho, né? Mas pode acontecer com qualquer um. Tenho conhecidos que trabalham nessa área de casamento, filmagem, fotos, e eles falaram que várias pessoas já passaram por isso. Foi mais um que desmaiou no dia da cerimônia", comentou.

Noiva chamou padrinhos e mãe para ajudar

Conforme contou Luana ao g1 , Jonathan começou a reclamar do calor durante a cerimônia, mesmo com o ar-condicionado ligado. Ao perceber que ele estava pálido e enfraquecendo, ela pediu ajuda aos padrinhos e à sogra.

O grupo deitou o noivo em um banco e ergueu as pernas dele. A sogra também passou água no rosto de Jonathan. Depois de uma primeira melhora, ele voltou a passar mal, e o casal decidiu continuar a celebração sentado.

Luana é técnica de enfermagem e contou que a presença de profissionais de saúde entre os convidados ajudou a deixá-la mais tranquila. Apesar do susto, o casal conseguiu aproveitar o restante da festa, que terminou às 23h.

Luana tem 37 anos e Jonathan, 36. Os dois se conheceram pelas redes sociais, estão juntos há seis anos e têm um filho de 3 anos.

articles.title: Tebbutt attack in Lamu: Kenyan Ali Kololo says Met Police ruined his life
articles.summary: Evidence from a British police officer helped convict Ali Kololo over a 2011 attack in the Kenyan resort of Lamu.
articles.body:
A Kenyan woodcutter who was wrongly convicted and sentenced to death over an attack on a British couple has told the BBC that actions by London's Metropolitan Police involved in the case destroyed his life.

Somali gunmen broke into David and Judith Tebbutt's beach bungalow on the Kenyan coast in 2011. They shot David dead and abducted Judith, holding her captive in Somalia for six months.

Met detectives flew to Kenya to assist the investigation. Their evidence helped convict Ali Kololo, who spent more than a decade in prison before his conviction was overturned.

Kololo is suing the Met, claiming a senior officer, former Detective Superintendent Neil Hibberd, gave misleading evidence at his trial and acted unlawfully to secure his conviction.

In his first media interview, he told the BBC about his 15-year ordeal and his fight for compensation, which the Met is challenging in court.

We meet on Lamu, a small island off Kenya's northern coast, once a thriving Swahili port. People and goods are still carted through its narrow stone streets by donkey rather than car.

It was here, in 2013, that Kololo was sentenced to death.

Standing at the jetty, where police once brought him ashore in handcuffs, he relishes being free. But he is struggling to rebuild his life.

"Everything was taken from me. I'm starting from zero. I don't think I'll ever go back to who I was before," he says.

Before his arrest, Kololo lived with his wife and their three young children. He had once worked as a groundskeeper at the resort where the Tebbutts were staying, but by 2011 he earned his living felling trees in a local forest and selling the wood.

"My life was very good," he says. "I was fending for myself, taking good care of my family."

Within 24 hours of the attack, Kenyan police had arrested him.

"I was beaten with clubs and thrown into a car," he says. "They beat me for days, burning me with cigarettes, forcing me to confess to things. They subjected me to torture like no other."

Kololo could not read or write. He says police made him put his thumbprint on a statement claiming he had led the attackers to the Tebbutts.

"I didn't understand anything," he says, calling the statement "a mountain of lies". "I signed it without knowing what it was because of the state they had put me in".

The Kenyan police told us it "at all times strives to work within the law". Kololo is not suing them.

Within days of the attack, a team of Met officers, led by then Detective Superintendent Neil Hibberd, arrived to support the Kenyan investigation. The UK government had instructed the officers not to accept information from the Kenyan authorities that had been obtained by interrogating detainees.

But Hibberd requested Kololo's statement and later relied on it when giving evidence for the prosecution at his trial.

In court, Hibberd also presented evidence linking Kololo to the attack. He told the Kenyan court Kololo had been wearing a type of shoe that matched footwear marks found in the sand at the resort.

The officer who had arrested Kololo said he was barefoot when he was handed to police. Hibberd did not disclose that the Met's own forensic examination could not establish whether the shoe in question had made the marks.

At the trial, Kololo did not initially have a lawyer. He had to cross-examine all the prosecution witnesses himself, including Hibberd, through an interpreter who spoke Swahili, which was not Kololo's first language.

"I believe I was framed because I am a poor man and I did not have the strength or means to fight for myself," Kololo says.

Kololo was convicted of kidnap and robbery with violence - the only person ever convicted in connection with the attack. He spent three years on death row before his sentence was commuted to life imprisonment.

He recalls seeing his prison file. In the space for the expiry date, someone had written "death".

"I was completely heartbroken. I believed I could be executed at any moment, and I would never see my family, my children, ever again."

Years later, the UK's Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) established that Hibberd had omitted significant forensic evidence at the trial. It found that he would have had a case to answer for gross misconduct, but he could not face disciplinary proceedings because he had retired from the force. At the time, his lawyer said Hibberd absolutely disagreed with the report's findings.

In April 2023, Kenya's High Court quashed Kololo's conviction, because of doubts over the prosecution's evidence. This followed years of work by the legal charity Reprieve and a Kenyan lawyer, Alfred Olaba, who represented him for free.

They were supported by Judith Tebbutt, who believed Kololo was innocent. In an interview with the BBC in 2022, she said he had been scapegoated by Scotland Yard.

"He was not there on the night. He was not part of the group that held me. They've put this man in prison without any real evidence."

More than three years after his release, Kololo says he is still living with the effects of his torture and decade in prison. As we walk the narrow streets of Lamu's old town, his thin frame moves stiffly. He is on edge. "My mind is not good," he says. "I have not recovered."

He remembers being kept in a filthy, bedbug-ridden cell with up to eight other inmates, which he thought he would never leave. Twice he contracted tuberculosis and nearly died.

Kololo is now too frail to do the woodcutting he once relied on to make a living. He tries to grow enough to eat on the land around his home, but erratic rain makes it difficult.

"I have nothing. On the days I get food, I eat, and on the days I don't, I endure."

He lives alone in a mud hut. His wife divorced him after he went to prison, and their children went to live with his mother. They dropped out of school because the family could not pay the fees. Kololo says they were not allowed to visit him in prison. When he was released, they barely remembered him, especially his youngest.

"They were too young. Only now are they starting to regain the memory that 'this is our father who disappeared'," he says. "If it weren't for my mother, my children might have died."

For much of our time together, Kololo is remarkably upbeat. He trusts that his lawyers and God will deliver him justice. But when we talk about the Met, his demeanour shifts.

"I am extremely angry with the police," he says. "I'm also angry with the Kenyan Police. They collaborated to incriminate me. What [Hibberd] said destroyed my entire life and my children's lives."

The Met has not apologised to Kololo or admitted wrongdoing. The force is contesting his compensation claim, which his lawyers say could take years to resolve.

"These people falsely accused me. Do I not deserve something?" he asks.

The Met told the BBC that neither they nor Hibberd wanted to comment on Kololo's claim, but it said: "Our thoughts are with Mr Kololo, Mrs Tebbutt, her family and all those who have been affected by this terrible crime. The Metropolitan Police remains committed to supporting the Kenyan authorities in any way that may be possible, in order to get justice for Mrs Tebbutt and her late husband."

Preetha Gopalan, Reprieve's head of UK litigation, describes the Met's behaviour in Kololo's case as "egregious".

"They've spent 10 years trying to evade accountability in every way possible, now dragging him through the courts," she says. "It's possible for them to do the right thing, but they are unwilling, and so this ordeal continues to haunt Kololo and his family."

"Even if I get a billion shillings, I will never be the same," Kololo says. "But if I get the justice I deserve, I can help my children and take care of myself when I am an old man."

articles.title: My self-care ritual is a meal at a fancy restaurant - on my own
articles.summary: Solo-dining is being embraced as a self-care trend and it's reshaping the restaurant industry.
articles.body:
Catherine Smith is perusing the menu at a high-end Mediterranean restaurant she has been excited to try. She has a new outfit on, and as she sips her rosé, she looks across at the empty seat opposite - bliss.

"I think what is so special about solo dining is that you don't have to wait for people to make those plans. You can go out and do them yourself," says the 23-year-old.

The self-confessed foodie is part of a growing trend of people booking tables for one - not because they're away with work but as a treat.

As food trends analyst Charles Banks puts it: "[Eating alone] is becoming an intentional act, a little pocket of independence, indulgence and self-care."

We spoke to solo dining fans and hospitality industry experts about how the trend is shaping the restaurant experience and asked if you would book a table for one.

Catherine, from Yorkshire, began dining solo at university and now does it at least once a month, choosing high-end restaurants she would not usually go to with friends and family.

She has been to a range of places both in the UK and abroad, doing "lots of research" to find new spots, typically spending £100 to £200 per meal.

"I think because a lot of my friends are vegan or vegetarian, I find that difficult sometimes because I'm quite a big meat eater," she says.

"I find it nice to be able to go out and pick a restaurant where I haven't had to scour through the menu to make sure that it's suitable for them."

Catherine says the sense of freedom she gets from picking where and when she eats "feels empowering".

"It definitely feels like not only a form of self-care but also a form of female liberation."

Online booking platform OpenTable says it covers more than 5,000 restaurants in the UK. It says solo dining makes up the smallest proportion of its bookings in the UK but it is the fastest-growing category.

Figures from 1 January to 31 August this year saw a rise of 23% in solo bookings compared to the same time period a year ago. It did not provide the data to the BBC to verify.

Nishi Singh was an avid solo diner when she lived in London, but found it wasn't widely accepted after moving to Delhi.

"Someone approached me and said that they assumed I'd been stood up," she tells BBC World Service's The Food Chain podcast.

"It sparked a conversation about the culture around solo dining in Delhi and I was really shocked to hear that it's not really something people do."

A couple of days later, she started documenting her solo dining experience on social media.

"Quite a lot of people have reached out and said that this is something they'd like to do and they're too scared to do it themselves," she says.

Banks, joint managing director of The Food People, a food trends and ideas agency, says that while solo dining isn't a "new consumer behaviour", changes in society mean it has become "almost aspirational".

But he notes that not every restaurant has welcomed the trend.

"A single diner could therefore feel like an inefficient use of a table rather than a customer the restaurant actively wanted."

SoloTable, a website that helps identify restaurants suitable for solo diners, found that one in eight of 178 restaurants it surveyed in London did not accept online reservations from solo diners.

Catherine says she has previously been turned away. "There are a lot of restaurants that I've wanted to go to before where they don't actually allow solo diners. And I've always found that to be really disappointing."

However, some restaurants like Jungli, an Indian restaurant in Newcastle upon Tyne, is working to attract solo diners.

Co-founder and director Yousaf Khalid has included high tables and bar seats in his recently opened restaurant. They also have charging points for laptops and phones.

"We want people to feel comfortable in these sorts of environments, being able to walk in on their own," he says.

He has hired staff with "bigger personalities" to engage customers in conversation but they also know when to leave diners alone if they want a more solitary experience.

Catherine urges anyone who fancies solo dining to give it a go.

"Food is a great way to bring people together, but it's also a great way to have good experiences on your own.

"I think with time, people will see and will start to accept it as something that's more normal."

Additional reporting by Jemma Crew and Emma Jackson.

articles.title: Georgia man accused of killing wife after dispute over children's Christmas presents
articles.summary: A Georgia man was charged with murder after police say he fatally shot his wife following an argument over Christmas presents for their four children.
articles.body: A Georgia man was arrested after allegedly shooting and killing his wife following an argument about Christmas presents they purchased for their four children. Gene McCall Allen, 33, was arrested Friday and charged with the murder of his wife of about eight years, Bonnie Lashea Allen, 32, according to the Walker County Sheriff's Office. He is being held at the Walker County Jail without bond. Deputies responded to the couple's home in Rossville, south of Chattanooga, Tennessee, on the evening of Nov. 14 following a report of a woman who had been shot, according to an incident report obtained by PEOPLE. Deputies found Gene Allen performing CPR on his wife, who had been shot in the head. A deputy also found a gun resting on a closet shelf facing toward the room, according to the report. MARATHONER ASKED HUSBAND ABOUT ‘POWDERY’ WATER BEFORE FATAL FALL – THEN POLICE FOUND HIS GOOGLE SEARCHES Gene Allen told deputies that the gun was inside the closet when it went off, PEOPLE reported. He also allegedly told authorities he and his wife argued earlier that day about the Christmas presents they bought for their children, saying she raised concerns about the cost of shipping and the quality of the gifts. The report also notes Gene Allen said he had four beers that day. Bonnie Allen's family created a GoFundMe to help the children with their everyday needs, including clothing, according to the fundraising site. Her children are now being cared for by family members. "Bonnie LaShae’s children & family [are] heartbroken over the tragic loss of a mother, daughter, sister, aunt and loved one who was taken far too soon. In the blink of an eye, her little children have lost their mother, and their lives have been changed forever," the fundraiser states. "No family should ever have to experience this kind of heartbreak, especially these little ones who have so much life ahead of them," it added. The GoFundMe has raised about $12,000 as of Thursday evening. In her obituary, Bonnie was remembered as "an amazing mother who never missed an opportunity to support her children." FLORIDA DEPUTY KILLED EX-GIRLFRIEND OVER A TV, THEN HIMSELF, SHERIFF SAYS "Whether cheering them on at a ball game or encouraging other children, she was always there, proudly showing her love and support. She was her children’s biggest fan, greatest encourager, and strongest supporter," the obituary reads. She was fun-loving, full of life, and always brought happiness wherever she went. A strong, natural leader, Bonnie had a way of encouraging others, making people feel welcome, and leaving a lasting impression on everyone she met. She will be remembered for her beautiful spirit, unwavering love for her family, her faith, and the joy she brought into so many lives," it added.

articles.title: Global news agency AFP reports cyberattack, shuts down content platform
articles.summary: France’s cybersecurity chief urges collective action to combat unprecedented threat levels in the nation.
articles.body:
Agence France-Presse (AFP) has been hit by a cyberattack, requiring the AFP Forum content platform to be taken offline.

The France-based international news agency’s management said on Thursday that it is currently investigating the circumstances of the cyberattack, including who was behind it.

“AFP was hit by a cyber attack overnight, starting at 1:30 am (Paris time) [00:30 GMT]. The target was AFP Forum, one of the platforms our clients use to browse and download our content,” an internal email from AFP management said.

“As soon as the intrusion was detected, our teams moved immediately to contain the intrusion and took AFP Forum offline as a precautionary measure. AFP Forum remains unavailable until further notice.”

AFP is reportedly offering backup solutions to the agency’s subscribers while the portal is offline.

France’s cybersecurity chief, Vincent Strubel, warned on Thursday that the country faces an unprecedented level of cybersecurity threats and called for collective efforts to strengthen defences against attacks.

“We are facing a level of threat that is unprecedented, with an intensity we have never experienced before,” Strubel said in an interview with France Inter radio.

The incident is the latest in a slew of cybersecurity disruptions across European countries. FIFA, which is based in Zurich, Switzerland, confirmed to Al Jazeera on Thursday that it had been the victim of a cyberattack that gave unauthorised access to personal and business information.

In October, several French supermarkets were hit by an “unprecedented” cyberattack that raised the temperature of fridges and freezers to as high as 50 degrees Celsius (122F).

Temperature spikes were also recorded in stores in 10 other European countries in early November, including the United Kingdom, Germany, Belgium and Sweden.

France accused Tehran of being behind the October attack and summoned Iran’s ambassador to Paris to “lodge a very strong protest”.

Iran called Paris’s accusations “baseless” and condemned the “hackneyed policy of levelling accusations against the Islamic republic”.

articles.title: TPUSA mourns Florida high school chapter president killed with family in devastating plane crash
articles.summary: Turning Point USA's student program is mourning Hunter Stokes, 16, who led its Fort Myers chapter, after the Cessna 210 he rode in crashed off Horn Island, Mississippi.
articles.body: Turning Point USA's student program mourned the death of a Florida high school chapter president this week after the teen and five members of his family died Tuesday in a plane crash off the Mississippi coast. The organization said it was "heartbroken" over the loss of Hunter Stokes, 16, who led the Fort Myers High School Club America chapter. "Hunter was a young patriot who loved his country and led by example," TPUSA Students said in a Wednesday post on X. SIX FLORIDA FAMILY MEMBERS KILLED IN PLANE CRASH ON WAY HOME FROM FISHING TRIP IDENTIFIED "From attending our Chapter Leadership Summit this summer to helping lead his chapter’s 9/11 Flag Run in honor of the victims of the September 11 attacks, Hunter was dedicated to making a difference in his community," the statement continued. "We are grateful to have had Hunter as part of our TPUSA family. Please join us in lifting his family, friends, and fellow chapter members up in prayer." Hunter was killed in the crash alongside his father, Brent Stokes, 50; his aunt and uncle, Arlyn and Michael Knox, both 43; and his cousins, Charles Holden Knox, 12, and Truett Knox, 10, according to Jackson County Coroner Bruce Lynd Jr. DOZENS MISSING AFTER PASSENGER FERRY SINKS AS RESCUERS SCOUR SOUTH PACIFIC COASTLINE GET BREAKING NEWS ALERTS The group was returning to Florida after a family fishing trip. "They died doing what they loved: celebrating the start of a wonderful holiday season with a fishing trip together, before heading home to be with the rest of our family," both families said in a joint statement to The News-Press. The six were aboard a Cessna 210 piloted by Brent Stokes when the aircraft went down two miles off Horn Island, Mississippi, according to the Federal Aviation Administration. Officials said the plane entered a descent of 10,000 feet per minute prior to the crash. GOT A TIP? Air traffic controllers advised Stokes of precipitation and adverse weather shortly before losing contact with the aircraft at about 3:45 p.m. local time, the New York Post and the FAA reported. Brent Stokes was the president and CEO of Stokes Marine Inc., while Arlyn and Michael Knox led Knox Technologies, an IT company based in Fort Myers. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP St. Cecilia Catholic Community on Wednesday said Brent and Hunter Stokes were former parishioners. "Please keep the Stokes and Knox families in your prayers during this time of loss," the community wrote in a Facebook post. "May the Lord grant eternal rest and the promise of the Resurrection. Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord, and let perpetual light shine upon them. May they rest in peace. Amen." The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Zelenskyy warns of major Russian attack as Trump urges Putin to ‘pull back’
articles.summary: Trump says he urged Putin to ‘pull back’ military aggression in Europe amid escalating Russian and Ukrainian attacks.
articles.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Ukraine has information that Russia is preparing a new mass strike on the country in the coming days.

“Unfortunately, we have information about a new mass strike being prepared by the Russians,” he said in his nightly video address on Thursday. “In the coming days, please pay attention to the alarms of missile threats.”

It was the second such warning from Zelenskyy this week. He also had a message for Moscow: “We will rebuild what is ours and retaliate against every Russian strike.”

US President Donald Trump said he had pressed Russian President Vladimir Putin to ease Russia’s military actions in Europe.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump said he spent “a lot of time” in talks with Putin in China on the issue of Putin pulling back “all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe”.

“Thousands of people are being killed each and every month, A COMPLETE BLOODBATH,” Trump wrote. He said he hoped that would allow a deal between Russia and Ukraine to be “made quickly”, which he called “a strong possibility”.

Trump said he updated NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte on the talks during a meeting at his Mar-a-Lago club in Florida on Wednesday night.

Russia struck Kyiv with ballistic missiles overnight, wounding seven people and hitting a shopping centre and two other buildings, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said.

Moscow said it hit drone-related sites in the city. Russian forces have attacked Kyiv and other cities almost continuously since September.

Ukraine said its drones hit an oil refinery in Russia’s southern Krasnodar region, oil reservoirs at a Transneft facility in Bashkortostan and the Marinovka military airfield in the Volgograd region.

Ukraine has also widened its attacks at sea. On Monday, Zelenskyy said Ukraine used seven naval drones to hit the Russian corvette Merkury and the cargo ship Angara off Libya . Libyan officials told the Associated Press news agency that the Merkury was heavily damaged but not sunk.

At about the same time, a suspected Ukrainian drone struck the Russia-bound cargo ship Sparta II in the Baltic Sea, near Finland. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov called the attacks a “ very dangerous trend “.

At least four Russian vessels have been targeted this month.

European Union leaders are struggling at a summit in Brussels to agree on a new 45 billion euro ($49bn) loan to help Ukraine meet its economic and military needs next year. It would come on top of a 90 billion euro ($99bn) loan , agreed nearly a year ago, that covers most of Ukraine’s government needs for 2026 and 2027.

Early on Friday in Brussels, European Council President Antonio Costa said that 24 member states supported the new loan , as talks on the bloc’s next seven-year budget stretched on.

The loan is tangled up with the EU’s budget for 2028 to 2034, which includes about $110bn for Ukraine over seven years. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has threatened to hold up the budget unless all member states make a “collective commitment” to Ukraine.

Ukraine’s military intelligence agency (GUR) said on Thursday that North Korea has temporarily halted some military cooperation with Russia after diplomatic tensions between the allies.

It said this includes deliveries of KN-23 ballistic missiles and artillery shells, and Russian military flights over North Korean territory.

GUR said North Korea’s Foreign Minister Choe Son-hui announced the pause last month in response to a Russian deputy foreign minister’s assertion that Moscow would help ease tensions between Seoul and Pyongyang.

GUR also said Pyongyang is holding off on a Russian request to raise North Korea’s military presence in Russia from about 8,500 to 50,000 troops.

It added that North Korean units remain in Russia’s Kursk region and that a North Korean missile unit has been in the Voronezh region since mid-summer, from where Russia strikes Ukraine.

South Korean and Western intelligence agencies have said Pyongyang sent more than 10,000 soldiers to Russia’s Kursk region in 2024, along with artillery shells, missiles and long-range rocket systems.

On November 20, Russia fired more than 400 drones and 110 missiles at Ukraine, killing eight people, Zelenskyy said.

It was one of the largest attacks of the war and followed Putin’s vow to retaliate for Ukrainian strikes on the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to Crimea.

articles.title: Putin's grip on Crimea tested amid major blackout as Zelenskyy warns of looming Russian strike
articles.summary: A massive blackout crippled Crimea, testing Vladimir Putin's grip as outages hit Sevastopol and Simferopol and Zelenskyy warned of a new Russian strike.
articles.body: Russian President Vladimir Putin's control over Crimea faced renewed pressure Thursday as a massive blackout crippled the Russian-occupied peninsula, disrupting public transport and leaving people without heat, according to reports. The blackout came after Ukrainian strikes had damaged the Kerch Strait Bridge last week, disrupting a key Russian military supply route, and as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Moscow was preparing another large-scale attack on Ukraine. Russian-controlled utilities blamed the Crimea blackout on an accident at energy facilities outside the region, after reports of explosions and air raid sirens sounded across the Black Sea peninsula, according to the Kyiv Post. PUTIN LAUNCHES UKRAINE BARRAGE HOURS AFTER TRUMP MEETING AMID ALLEGED RUSSIAN MISSILE BREACH OF NATO AIRSPACE Meanwhile, Zelenskyy said Ukrainian intelligence suggested that Russia was preparing to target the country's energy infrastructure, logistics networks and essential services. "Unfortunately, the Russians are already completing preparations for a new massive strike," Zelenskyy wrote on X Thursday following a coordination meeting. "According to intelligence, energy facilities and logistics infrastructure, as well as essential services facilities in cities and communities, will once again be the targets." The Ukrainian leader also urged residents to remain vigilant, warning of renewed missile attacks. "In the coming days, please pay attention to the alarms of missile threats," Zelenskyy said in his nightly video address Thursday, according to Reuters. "And in Russia, they should know that we will rebuild what is ours and retaliate against every Russian strike." In Crimea, Russian-controlled electricity provider Sevastopolenergo said that Sevastopol had lost power, while electricity restrictions affected Simferopol, Kerch, Alushta and Yevpatoria, according to Ukrainian news outlet Ukrainska Pravda. ZELENSKYY SAYS RUSSIA STRIKES HOMETOWN, CRITICIZES PUTIN-TRUMP MEETING Streetcar services were also suspended in Yevpatoria and buses replaced trolleybuses on some routes in Simferopol. Parts of Kerch were also reportedly left without heating. Russian-installed authorities had issued air raid alerts Thursday morning amid reports of explosions. The blackout is the latest in a series of disruptions that have hit Crimea since late October, with Russian authorities blaming damage to power infrastructure. The disruptions come amid mounting pressure on Crimea, which Moscow annexed in 2014 and has since used as a military and logistics hub for its operations against Ukraine. The Kerch Strait Bridge, which connects the peninsula to mainland Russia, serves as a critical transportation link for Russian forces and has been targeted by Ukraine since Putin launched his invasion in 2022. KUSHNER ENTERS UKRAINE PEACE TALKS AS TRUMP EYES SECURING SAFEGUARDS AGAINST ANOTHER RUSSIAN INVASION The bridge was built after the Russian annexation and opened in 2018, serving as a symbol of Moscow's control over the peninsula. Meanwhile in Kyiv, Mayor Vitali Klitschko also said seven people were wounded in an overnight Russian attack on the Ukrainian capital that damaged a shopping center and two other buildings, Reuters reported. Zelenskyy also called for additional air defense assistance Thursday, emphasizing the need for interceptors for Patriot air defense systems and National Advanced Surface-to-Air Missile Systems (NASAMS). "I expect a report from Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry on the results of its communication with our partners regarding the supply of air defenses — interceptors for Patriots and NASAMS are the key priority," Zelenskyy wrote. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP It was the second time this week Zelenskyy had warned of preparations for another major Russian attack, according to Reuters.

articles.title: Trump downplays Russia, China support for Iran during talks with US troops
articles.summary: Trump praises US troops for their role in the war on Iran and says he has spoken to Netanyahu in recent days.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump has claimed Iran possesses missiles capable of reaching Europe and downplayed Russia and China’s support for Tehran while speaking to US military personnel by phone for the Thanksgiving holiday.

Taking questions from reporters at his Mar-a-Lago residence in Florida on Thursday, Trump said without “peace in the Middle East”, Iran could launch nuclear attacks against Israel and other countries in the region.

“We don’t need Middle East oil. But what we do need is we need peace in the Middle East,” Trump said, as OPEC ministers are scheduled to meet on Sunday to weigh 2027 oil production targets.

The US president and First Lady Melania Trump called US service members deployed across the region to praise their role in the war on Iran, including personnel at the al-Dhafra airbase in the United Arab Emirates and the Prince Sultan airbase in Saudi Arabia.

“Each of you is playing an essential role to protect not only our country today but future generations of Americans by ensuring that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon,” he said.

When asked if the US would renew strikes on Iran, the president said: “If we do something, we will definitely hit Pickaxe Mountain.” Trump also told reporters he spoke with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in recent days.

The US is still offering Iran an opening to negotiate, according to Trump, who said: “We’re trying to be nice. We’re giving them every chance to make a deal and save a lot of lives, but I’m not sure if they are gonna take advantage of that.”

He downplayed the importance of intelligence-sharing by Russia and China with Iran, amid reports that the two countries helped Tehran target US bases.

“My meeting with President Xi was an incredible meeting. I think that they’re very little involved with Iran. They could get involved, but involvement to me would mean shooting, not giving them little information,” Trump said during the short news conference.

“We do the same thing, by the way. And you know, when they say that they may be spying on us, well, we spy on them too,” he added.

Trump’s statements come as Iran steps up attacks on US military targets across the region. On Saturday, Bahrain reported an Iranian attack on a civilian industrial facility while Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed it targeted US air defence radars in the country.

Kuwait said on Thursday that an Iranian drone attack on a “vital site” killed two Italian workers and injured four others. Tehran has denied involvement in the attack.

Trump told deployed service members, “You’re going to continue that deployment, and we have victory at hand,” referring to the war on Iran.

“It’s [victory] going to be whenever I want it to be, to be honest,” he added.

articles.title: Zelensky on Trump calling Putin ‘friend’: ‘Same as somebody saying about Hitler’ in WWII
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said President Trump calling Russian President Vladimir Putin a “friend” was the “same as somebody saying about Hitler” in World War II. When asked during a BBC interview how he felt about Trump’s comment about Putin, Zelensky stated “it’s up to the President of the United States, but it’s strange.” Putin…
articles.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said President Trump calling Russian President Vladimir Putin a “ friend ” was the “same as somebody saying about Hitler” in World War II.

When asked during a BBC interview how he felt about Trump’s comment about Putin, Zelensky stated “it’s up to the President of the United States, but it’s strange.”

Putin was “an aggressor and a killer. He can’t be a friend, a friend. Just cannot be. It’s the same that somebody say about Hitler during the Second World War that he is a good friend. No, he is not a friend,” Zelensky continued.

Trump called Putin his “friend” right before the pair walked into a room with Chinese President Xi Jinping. The president has enjoyed an amicable relationship with his Russian counterpart, especially with recent trilateral talks in Shenzhen, China.

Trump signaled previously that he wanted the Russian-Ukraine war to end, as the conflict will reach the five-year mark in February.

In his BBC interview, Zelensky expressed he felt there needed to be “more progress” in U.S.-backed peace talks between the countries.

“We need the American position to be American position. We don’t need signals,” he said.

Zelensky pushed for the U.S. to put “pressure on the situation” especially as he believed “Russia is the aggressor, so that’s why they have to do it.”

“It’s not about comfortable talks. It’s about strong country who can pressure because this country has power and respect,” he concluded.

The Ukrainian president has previously called for the U.S. and European partners to provide Patriot missile interceptors , which he stated are paramount to shooting down Russian missiles and drones targeting the country’s cities.

Recent Russian strikes hit an apartment building north of Kyiv on Sunday. The attacks killed at least four people and left up to a dozen more buried in the rubble.

U.S. special envoy Jared Kushner, Trump’s son-in-law, said the talks are “ making progress ” toward ending the conflict, but some challenges still remain. One challenge Kushner and fellow special envoy Steve Witkoff have faced is struggling to include European partners in peace talks.

articles.title: Thanksgiving storms leave nearly a million without power across the US
articles.summary: Severe weather across the US causes outages and flight delays as families and friends gather for the annual holiday.
articles.body:
Strong winds and heavy storms have knocked out power for nearly a million US homes and businesses and resulted in the rare postponement of Macy’s annual Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City.

As Americans marked the annual holiday on Thursday, heavy storms disrupted travel across the country, with more than 2,000 flights to or from US destinations delayed and more than 400 cancelled, according to the flight tracking service FlightAware.

More than 900,000 homes and businesses were without electricity on Thursday evening, with the majority in East Coast states, according to the outage tracking website poweroutage.us. New Jersey and parts of New York were placed under a state of emergency.

The US National Weather Service issued wind advisories for northern Georgia, the majority of the mid-Atlantic and southern New England.

Two people were rescued from their cars in New York City due to flooding, according to Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

“There is no destination worth your safety,” Mamdani said. Similar rescues were reported in other coastal communities.

In Maryland, nearly two million water customers in Montgomery and Prince George’s counties were asked to conserve water because of intermittent power disruptions related to heavy rain. The storms also prompted several brief tornado warnings, including for a rare twister southeast of Seattle, Washington.

The Midwestern region witnessed heavy snowfall on Thursday, with some areas of Missouri recording up to 35cm of snow.

Meanwhile, waves driven by high tides caused flooding along the Pacific coast. The conditions were expected to continue into Friday, according to the National Weather Service.

Record tides along the California coast forced evacuations in areas from Humboldt County in the far north to southern Ventura County near Los Angeles.
